1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.f4.strategy: Defends the e5 pawn and takes a big space advantage. White commits the kingside to the pawn chain and loosens the e3 square and the king's diagonal. Black has a clear target in the base of the chain at d4.

1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.Nc.strategy: Reroutes the knight so that both the c-pawn and the f-pawn can advance to support the centre, while the knight guards d4 and the f4 square. It is a slower, solid set-up that gives up the knight's pressure on d5 and e4 and lags in development.
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.Nc.name: French Defence: Classical Variation, Shirov-Anand Variation

1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.Qg.strategy: An early queen sortie that hits g7 and e6, but both are guarded, so it makes no real threat. It spends a tempo and gives Black time to strike at the d4 pawn.
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.Qg.name: French Defence: Steinitz Variation, Gledhill Attack

1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.f4.strategy: Undermines the base of the pawn chain at once: if d4 falls, the e5 pawn loses its support and the knight takes it. White has to keep defending d4, which slows the rest of White's development.
